title: Saturating tenant burst protection and telemetry gaps
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a hosted inference capacity event on 2026-02-09 we observed rapid queue buildup driven by a small subset of tenants issuing large short-lived bursts. Existing admission controls and autoscaler priming did not prevent transient GPU pool saturation. Key root causes: (1) tenant-level burst traffic bypassed coarse admission windows, amplifying queue growth; (2) telemetry blind spots in per-tenant recent-burst counters meant throttles were reacting too late; (3) KV cache and prewarm heuristics did not prioritize hot prefixes, increasing per-request GPU work and reducing throughput. This ticket consolidates follow-up work: an adaptive tenant burst protector (short-window token-bucket + escalation fingerprints), richer telemetry for burst detection, KV cache prefetch improvements targeted at bursty prefixes, and a staged rollout with canary + fast rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive tenant burst protector implemented and enabled behind a runtime feature flag
Telemetry surfaced showing 1s and 5s per-tenant burst-rate metrics in Console and alerting on sustained burst > threshold
KV cache prefetch changes reduce average per-token GPU latency for identified hot prefixes by >= 15% in canary pool
Automated chaos/soak test demonstrating queue stays below safety watermark under synthetic tenant bursts
Runbook updated with detection thresholds, mitigation steps, and escalation contacts
notes_or_comments: 2026-02-11: Initial triage — incident IN-2026-02-09-07. Observed 3x baseline RPS for 15 minutes from 4 tenants; one tenant single request pattern caused 10x KV cache misses. Logged sampling artifacts to s3://redwood-incidents/IN-2026-02-09-07.

2026-02-12: Telemetry gap identified: per-tenant 1s-rate not emitted to metrics pipeline; team decision: add lightweight per-tenant ring counters (Prom push gateway + rollup) to reduce ingestion cost.

2026-02-14: Design review — tradeoffs discussed. Option A: global stricter admission window (simple but hurts steady-state throughput). Option B: per-tenant short-window token-bucket + weight decay (more complex but targeted). PM prefers B. Engineering to prototype B first.

2026-02-16: Prototype completed by @Marco Greene. Token-bucket on request admission with a 5s bucket size + emergency throttle at 30s sustained burst. Early bench shows 40% reduction in peak queue depth in sim.
2026-02-18: KV cache change: prefetch prioritization added for top-40 hot prefixes using LRU + burst-weight; PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4512.
2026-02-20: Telemetry PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/1226 — emits per-tenant short-window counters and sample of admission-drop reasons. Need ops signoff for retention/alerts.

2026-02-22: Security review flagged minor PII concern in sampled request traces; sampling reduced and KMS encryption enforced for event archives. Security sign-off pending but not blocking feature flag rollout.
2026-02-24: QA discovered a corner-case where very low-volume tenants can be overthrottled due to mis-specified decay window; will be fixed by adding minimum allowance for tenants < 1 req/min.

2026-02-25: SRE planning for staged rollout: canary on dedicated canary GPU pool (10% traffic), 24h observation window, automatic rollback if queue watermark breached or customer error % increases > 0.5%.
2026-02-26: PM note — communicate to top 50 tenants about upcoming enforcement window and opt-in for testing to reduce surprise. Engagement owner assigned: Priya Nair (account exec).
